solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A top case for Sherlock Holmes?

definitions.text: A top case for Sherlock Holmes?

blocks.note: not a first-rate mystery but a case in the sense of a covering, one for the top of the head
the detective's trademark headgear in the illustrations, with flaps front and back

explanation.walkthrough: "Case for Sherlock Holmes" sounds like one of his mysteries, but a "top case" is a covering for the top of the head: the hat he is always drawn wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A DEERSTALKER is the peaked cloth cap famously worn by Sherlock Holmes in illustrations.

clue.text: Desperate man, 101, no good doing the foxtrot maybe

blocks.note: Desperate Dan, the strongman of the British comic The Dandy
CI is 101 in Roman numerals
NG is the standard abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A man at the end of his tether, a hundred and one years old and useless, trying a ballroom dance.
explanation.walkthrough: "Desperate" looks like an anagram signal for MAN, but there is no M in the answer: Desperate Dan is a well-known British comic-strip character.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxtrot is one kind of dance, so someone doing it is DANCING; "maybe" marks the example.

clue.text: One’s paid a student — pounds wasted!

blocks.note: a student is a LEARNER
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Someone paid a student and complains that the money was thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: "One's paid" reads as "one has paid"; it is really "one who is paid", a noun phrase for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: whoever receives a wage for work earns it.

clue.text: Very powerful men rush up excitedly, enthralling Anne initially

indicators.note: men rushing up excitedly are in disorder, so their letters are jumbled
Anne initially is the first letter of Anne
to enthral is to hold captive, so the jumble holds the A inside it

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the first letter of Anne

explanation.surface: A crowd of men dashes excitedly towards Anne, who holds them spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: The A from Anne slots in near the end of the rearranged letters, between SUPERHUM and N.
explanation.definitionFit: SUPERHUMAN means having powers beyond the human, that is very powerful.

clue.text: Shrewd maiden leaving protest movement?

indicators.note: the maiden walks out of the march, so her letter goes

blocks.note: a protest march
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A clever young woman quits the protest movement, perhaps with second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: ARCH can mean knowing, sly or shrewd, as in an arch look.

clue.text: Brute upset a top man participating in water sport

indicators.note: in a down clue something upset is turned upside down

blocks.note: a yak is a large beast, a brute in the animal sense
the A as printed
the king is the man at the top

explanation.surface: A thug has capsized the boss during a water sport.
explanation.walkthrough: "Brute" means a beast here, not a thug; the yak is the crossword's favourite beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: paddling a small covered canoe is one sport done on water.

clue.text: Embarrassed about fatigue, gave up work

indicators.note: "about" in its sense of around: the embarrassed colour surrounds the fatigue

blocks.note: red-faced with embarrassment
to fatigue is to TIRE

explanation.surface: Someone ashamed of being tired out has left their job.
explanation.walkthrough: "Embarrassed" and "fatigue" look like one feeling described twice; they are two separate pieces, one wrapped round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: leaving employment for good, usually in old age.

clue.text: May stumble on account of old trick

blocks.note: "may" in the sense of being permitted, as in "you can go"
to stumble is to TRIP

explanation.surface: Someone may fall over because of an old prank.
explanation.walkthrough: "May" at the start looks like the month; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: CANTRIP is an old Scottish word for a spell or a mischievous trick.

clue.text: Put into boxes in iced storage possibly

indicators.note: the letters of iced storage are possibly in another order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Food packed into boxes and kept in the freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: "Put into boxes" is figurative: placed in categories.
explanation.definitionFit: To be CATEGORISED is to be sorted into classes, figuratively put into boxes.

clue.text: Like this crossword? It makes one weep, quietly twitching!

blocks.note: to weep is to CRY
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
a tic is a nervous twitching

explanation.surface: A solver jokes that this crossword is so hard it makes them sob and twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: P, for piano, is the usual crossword shorthand for quietly; the question mark admits the definition points at the puzzle itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-reference: the puzzle being solved is of the puzzling, hidden-meaning kind, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: One plotting studies holy men, rotter infiltrating

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
PI is short for pious
a rat is a rotter, a contemptible person
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A schemer studies monks while a traitor works his way in among them.
explanation.walkthrough: "Holy men" looks like one unit such as priests or saints; it is two separate words. OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who plots in secret with others.

clue.text: Cosmetic material needing an effort

blocks.note: toile is a light linen or cotton fabric
a try is an attempt, an effort

explanation.surface: Applying some make-up substance takes real effort.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cosmetic material" reads as one phrase, but "material" is the fabric TOILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic, as a noun, is a TOILETRY such as a cream or lotion.

clue.text: Slope outside to accommodate sport

blocks.note: the skin is the outside of something
RU is Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A hillside out of doors is being adapted to host some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: "Outside" looks like a container signal; here it is a noun, the SKIN that does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the answer is one particular kind of slope, a prepared piste on a mountain.

clue.text: Get salt sprinkled, catching one insect and another

definitions.note: stands for "another insect", carrying on from the insect in the wordplay

indicators.note: salt that is sprinkled is scattered, so the letters of get salt scatter

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a bee is an insect

explanation.surface: A recipe step: scatter salt, trapping a couple of bugs in the process.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just "another": the bee is one insect, and the answer is another one.
explanation.definitionFit: A STAG BEETLE is a large beetle with antler-like jaws, another insect.

clue.text: Fatuous joke suitable for adults once

blocks.note: a gag is a joke
A was the old British film certificate for adult audiences

explanation.surface: A silly joke that used to be considered adult material.
explanation.walkthrough: British films were once rated A, meaning adults should accompany children; "once" says the rating is no longer used.
explanation.definitionFit: GAGA means foolish or senile, so fatuous.

clue.text: Uncommunicative, but made more vigorous

blocks.note: BUT as printed
muscles made more vigorous are TONED UP

explanation.surface: Someone became quieter yet fitter.
explanation.walkthrough: "but" looks like a link between two ideas; it is the first three letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone BUTTONED-UP keeps their thoughts to themselves, so is uncommunicative.

clue.text: Engineers wanting stock control

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
a strain is a breed or line of descent, a stock

explanation.surface: Army engineers who need supplies want to take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stock" suggests goods in store; here it is lineage, as in a strain of wheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to hold back or keep in check.

clue.text: Finger real twitchy? It’s on the trigger here

definitions.text: Finger real twitchy? It’s on the trigger here

indicators.note: a twitchy finger jerks about, so its letters and those of real are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A nervous shooter with a really jumpy trigger finger.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the place: a twitchy finger is on the trigger at a RIFLE RANGE, where shooters practise.
explanation.definitionFit: A RIFLE RANGE is where people practise shooting, fingers on the trigger.

clue.text: Goods bringing sudden fear — drug smuggled therein

indicators.note: the drug is sneaked inside the fright

blocks.note: a fright is a sudden fear
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A cargo causes panic when drugs are found hidden inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: E, for ecstasy, is the crossword's usual drug.
explanation.definitionFit: FREIGHT is goods carried by lorry, ship or plane.

clue.text: Top man hugged by sweet Sarah

indicators.note: the answer is held tight within the words sweet Sarah

blocks.note: sweeT SARah

explanation.surface: The boss gets a cuddle from lovely Sarah.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian emperor stood at the top; the word is also used loosely for anyone put in charge, like a drugs tsar.

clue.text: Credulously believe a flighty type

blocks.note: to take a tall story in whole, as if gulping it down
a creature of flight, a migrating bird with a forked tail

explanation.walkthrough: "Flighty" usually means fickle; here it is literal, a creature that flies. The answer is SWALLOW, gulping down a story and the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb's figurative sense of accepting without question, and the noun for the fork-tailed bird.

clue.text: It can be very warm and wet outside the chalet

definitions.text: It can be very warm and wet outside the chalet

blocks.clueFragment: It can be very warm and wet
blocks.note: reads like the weather, but describes a thing full of heated water
placed out on the deck of a ski lodge, where guests soak after the slopes

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a weather report for a mountain holiday; the very warm, wet thing outside the chalet is the heated bath on the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A HOT TUB is an outdoor heated pool, a fixture of ski chalets.

clue.text: Wet — say, after working

indicators.note: letters that are working are moving about, so wet say is rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is damp, you might say, after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: wet, so to speak, after working is exactly what SWEATY describes.
explanation.definitionFit: SWEATY means damp with sweat, the way one is after working hard.

clue.text: Vibrant English boy in verbal onslaught

indicators.note: "in" places the English boy inside the onslaught

blocks.note: a rant is a verbal onslaught
E is the abbreviation for English
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lively English lad caught in the middle of a tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: Both E and SON go inside the rant together, E first.
explanation.definitionFit: RESONANT means deep and ringing, vibrant in sound.

clue.text: House in Home Counties north of motorway

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece north of another sits above it

blocks.note: the Home Counties surround London in the South East of England
the M1, written MI, is Britain's main north-south motorway

explanation.surface: A home in the commuter belt just off the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in the South East; the M1 motorway is MI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A SEMI is a semi-detached house, one of a pair sharing a wall, typical of British suburbs.

clue.text: University ambition cut short, a daughter admitted disgrace

indicators.note: the degree is cut short, losing its last letter
"admitted" in its sense of let in: the shortened degree lets the daughter enter

blocks.note: a student's ambition is a degree
the A as printed
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A student's hopes of a degree end early when their daughter owns up to a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: "Admitted" reads as confessed in the surface; in the wordplay it means let in.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to bring someone low in others' esteem.

clue.text: Being like a guardian that’s awful, real weird!

indicators.note: real made weird comes out in a strange order

blocks.note: TUT is the click of disapproval, a way of saying that's awful
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a guardian's behaviour is dreadful and truly strange.
explanation.walkthrough: TUT is the click of disapproval, written as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: TUTELAR means relating to a guardian or protector, so being like a guardian.

clue.text: Inflammation after game? Be silent now, suffering

indicators.note: the letters are in pain and twisted out of shape

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sore player is told to stop complaining and put up with the pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennis elbow is a strain injury of the forearm tendons; the question mark admits a game of tennis is only one cause.
explanation.definitionFit: TENNIS ELBOW is inflammation of the elbow tendons, the sort of thing you get after a game; "?" flags the loose definition.
